name: Minnesota
overview: In Minnesota a facility needs an air permit when its potential to emit exceeds a permitting threshold, unless it is an insignificant facility or a conditionally exempt source. State permits for minor sources include one-page registration permits, capped emission permits, a state general permit, and individual state total facility permits. Federal permits are Part 70 individual permits and a Part 70 manufacturing general permit. Rules are in Minn. R. ch. 7007 (permits) and ch. 7008 (conditionally exempt sources).

permitTypes.name: Insignificant facilities and conditionally exempt sources
permitTypes.description: Insignificant facilities may not need a permit (MPCA offers a PTE calculator). Conditionally exempt sources (e.g., auto body, coating, woodworking, gasoline stations, concrete manufacturers) may exceed thresholds but follow technical standards and usually notify MPCA instead of getting a permit.

permitTypes.name: Registration Permits (incl. Option D)
permitTypes.description: One-page, non-expiring state permits for facilities whose actual emissions are low compared to potential (generally under 50% of federal thresholds). Not available to acid rain sources, waste combustors, or facilities with SIP requirements or certain NSPS.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per MPCA (Option D, actual emissions): under 50 tpy each of PM, PM10, VOC, SO2, NOx, CO; under 5 tpy single HAP; under 12.5 tpy all HAPs; under 0.5 tpy lead; under 50,000 tpy CO2e.

permitTypes.name: Capped Emission Permit
permitTypes.description: Caps facility-wide emissions to stay below Part 70 or NSR major thresholds; changes allowed without amendment while under the cap. Single-page permit.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per MPCA: actual emissions under 75%-90% of federal thresholds (e.g., Option 1 under 90 tpy listed pollutants including insignificant activities).

permitTypes.name: State General Permit
permitTypes.description: One state general permit is currently available, for non-metallic mineral processing.

permitTypes.name: Individual State Total Facility Permit
permitTypes.description: Facility-specific permit with limits to remain minor for NSR and Part 70; 30-day public notice; five-year term; amendments required for changes.

permitTypes.name: PSD / NSR
permitTypes.description: Major NSR applies at 100 or 250 tpy depending on source category; individual Part 70 permits often include limits to remain minor for NSR.

permitTypes.name: Part 70 Individual and General Permits
permitTypes.description: Individual permits for the largest facilities (30-day public comment, 45-day EPA review, five-year renewal). A Part 70 general permit covers manufacturing facilities.

oilAndGas.summary: Minnesota has no oil and gas production. MPCA's permit pages list no oil-and-gas-specific air program; stationary engine guidance applies to compressor and generator engines.
